key_insight: Denoising diffusion models generate realistic additive-manufacturing microstructure images and enable inverse mappings from target properties or process conditions to microstructures.
engineering_relevance: Generative microstructure models could support CPFEM-based digital twins and uncertainty quantification to accelerate metal AM qualification.
method: Train denoising diffusion probabilistic models to synthesize orientation-imaging micrographs.
Use classifier-free guidance for property-to-structure and process-to-structure inverse mappings.
Demonstrate a qualification-relevant uncertainty quantification application.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative evidence of generated-sample fidelity but provides no dataset sizes, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
watch_item: Image fidelity alone does not establish mechanical predictive accuracy; generated microstructures need validation in downstream CPFEM workflows.
paper_title: Microstructural Generative Inverse Models for Additive Manufacturing Digital Twins
